problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=-\frac{1}{4}t,\,y=-\frac{1}{8}{t}^{2},\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=4t,\,y=2{t}^{2},\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}t & =\frac{x}{4},\,{t}^{2}=\frac{1}{2}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the first equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=\frac{1}{2}y$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{16} & =\frac{1}{2}y \\ {x}^{2} & =8y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian equation of the parabola is ${x}^{2}=8y.$
